name: The congregation, the day after Korah
charge: Murmuring that Moses and Aaron had killed the people of the Lord
summary: The earth had swallowed Korah’s company the day before and the fire had consumed the two hundred and fifty, and on the very next day the whole congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron and called the dead the people of the Lord. Wrath went out from the Lord and the plague began before any warning. Aaron, the high priest they had said was no better than themselves, ran with a censer and stood between the dead and the living. Fourteen thousand seven hundred died, and his rod that budded was laid up as a token against the rebels.
offenseFull: On the next day the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying that they had killed the people of the Lord (Numbers 16:41). After they had just seen the earth open and swallow men alive and fire come out and consume the rest, they still would not let it go. Look at who was blamed. Who opened the earth? Moses did not open it; God did, and they laid the dead at the feet of the two men who had pleaded for them. That is our habit as a people: when a man is checked for his own fault, he looks for somebody else to blame. And the ones who stood by were glad their names had not been in the first company, not understanding that the Most High had their number too, and had it the very next day.

The judgment they had watched became the grievance, and the Most High saw what was going on: the cloud covered the tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord appeared (Numbers 16:42-45). He came down ready to put them to death again, telling Moses and Aaron to get up from among the congregation so that He could consume them in a moment; and Moses and Aaron fell on their faces, still pleading for their people. That is the character of the man: no matter what was said against him, he loved his people and stood up for them. Paul warns not to murmur as some of them murmured and were destroyed of the destroyer (1 Corinthians 10:10).
judgmentFull: Wrath had gone out from the Lord and the plague was begun before any test or warning. Moses told Aaron to take a censer, put fire in it from off the altar and incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation to make an atonement for them (Numbers 16:46). Aaron ran into the midst of the congregation, put on incense, and made an atonement for the people; he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed (Numbers 16:47-48). The high priest they had said was no better than themselves stood in the gap with the very fire the two hundred and fifty had died for offering. Those who died in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in the matter of Korah (Numbers 16:49-50).

Then the Lord settled the question so that it would not have to be settled with bodies again. Every prince wrote his name on his rod according to the house of his fathers, twelve rods, with Aaron’s name on the rod of Levi, and they were laid up before the testimony where the Lord met with them; the man whose rod blossomed was the man He had chosen (Numbers 17:2-9). On the morrow the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi had budded, brought forth buds, bloomed blossoms and yielded almonds, and every man took back his own rod. Aaron’s rod was brought again before the testimony to be kept as a token against the rebels, to take their murmurings away from the Lord so that they would not die, and Moses did as he was commanded (Numbers 17:10-11). The children of Israel cried that they were dying and perishing, all of them, and that any man who came near the tabernacle of the Lord would die (Numbers 17:12-13). A man had to be of Levi to go near it; that had to be his office.

text.text: But on the morrow all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of the Lord.

And it came to pass, when the congregation was gathered against Moses and against Aaron, that they looked toward the tabernacle of the congregation: and, behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle of the congregation.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Get you up from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment. And they fell upon their faces.
Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.

And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and put on incense, and go quickly unto the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from the Lord; the plague is begun.
And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and, behold, the plague was begun among the people: and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people.
And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
Now they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside them that died about the matter of Korah.
And Aaron returned unto Moses unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the plague was stayed.

Speak unto the children of Israel, and take of every one of them a rod according to the house of their fathers, of all their princes according to the house of their fathers twelve rods: write thou every man’s name upon his rod.
And thou shalt write Aaron’s name upon the rod of Levi: for one rod shall be for the head of the house of their fathers.
And thou shalt lay them up in the tabernacle of the congregation before the testimony, where I will meet with you.
And it shall come to pass, that the man’s rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel, whereby they murmur against you.

And Moses spake unto the children of Israel, and every one of their princes gave him a rod apiece, for each prince one, according to their fathers’ houses, even twelve rods: and the rod of Aaron was among their rods.
And Moses laid up the rods before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness.

And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.
And Moses brought out all the rods from before the Lord unto all the children of Israel: and they looked, and took every man his rod.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Bring Aaron’s rod again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels; and thou shalt quite take away their murmurings from me, that they die not.
And Moses did so: as the Lord commanded him, so did he.
And the children of Israel spake unto Moses, saying, Behold, we die, we perish, we all perish.
Whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of the Lord shall die: shall we be consumed with dying?
